unverifiedDraft.tagline: The second Sikh Guru who standardized Gurmukhi script, established community wrestling arenas, and personified utter devotion.
unverifiedDraft.taglineLocal: द्वितीय सिख गुरु जिन्होंने गुरुमुखी लिपि व्यवस्थित की, मल्ल अखाड़े बनाए और सेवा का शिखर प्रस्तुत किया।
unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਦੂਜੇ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਗੁਰਮੁਖੀ ਲਿਪੀ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਣਿਤ ਕੀਤੀ, ਮੱਲ ਅਖਾੜੇ ਬਣਾਏ ਅਤੇ ਸੇਵਾ-ਸਮਰਪਣ ਦੀ ਮਿਸਾਲ ਕਾਇਮ ਕੀਤੀ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Born as Bhai Lehna, his spiritual longing brought him to Kartarpur Sahib after hearing Guru Nanak's hymns. He abandoned worldly prestige to perform tireless service, cleaning stables, carrying dripping mud, and seeing only the Divine in his Master. Guru Nanak designated him his successor, naming him Angad—a limb of his own being. At Khadur Sahib, Guru Angad developed the Gurmukhi alphabet to record Gurbani, fostered physical fitness among youth through wrestling, and with Mata Khivi expanded the egalitarian Langar.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: भाई लहणा जी गुरु नानक देव जी की वाणी सुनकर करतारपुर पहुंचे और अपना सर्वस्व समर्पित कर दिया। उन्होंने बिना किसी झिझक के कठिन से कठिन सेवा की। गुरु नानक देव जी ने उन्हें अपना अंग मानकर 'अंगद' नाम दिया और गुरुपद सौंपा। खड़ूर साहिब में गुरु अंगद देव जी ने गुरुमुखी लिपि का प्रसार किया, मल्ल अखाड़ों की स्थापना की और माता खीवी जी के साथ लंगर सेवा को सुदृढ़ किया।
unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਭਾਈ ਲਹਿਣਾ ਜੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਕਰਕੇ ਕਰਤਾਰਪੁਰ ਟਿਕ ਗਏ ਅਤੇ ਅਥਾਹ ਸੇਵਾ ਨਿਭਾਈ। ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੇ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣਾ ਅੰਗ ਜਾਣ ਕੇ ਗੁਰਗੱਦੀ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ੀ। ਆਪ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਗੁਰਮੁਖੀ ਲਿਪੀ ਪ੍ਰਚਲਿਤ ਕੀਤੀ, ਸਰੀਰਕ ਤੰਦਰੁਸਤੀ ਲਈ ਮੱਲ ਅਖਾੜੇ ਕਾਇਮ ਕੀਤੇ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਤਾ ਖੀਵੀ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਦੇਖ-ਰੇਖ ਵਿੱਚ ਲੰਗਰ ਦਾ ਵਿਸਥਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ।
unverifiedDraft.trial: Underwent severe tests of humility and obedience, from retrieving a bowl from freezing mud at night to unhesitatingly following commands that bewildered all others.
unverifiedDraft.trialLocal: शीत ऋतु की रात्रि में दलदल से बर्तन निकालना और गुरु-आज्ञा पर बिना संकोच सर्वस्व न्योछावर करना उनकी सर्वोच्च परीक्षा थी।
unverifiedDraft.trialPa: ਠੰਢੀ ਰਾਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਚਿੱਕੜ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਲੋਟਾ ਕੱਢਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੇ ਹਰ ਬਚਨ ਨੂੰ ਅੱਖਾਂ ਮੀਟ ਕੇ ਮੰਨਣਾ ਆਪ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਕਠਿਨ ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ ਸੀ।
unverifiedDraft.teaching: Ego is eliminated only when selfless service merges into wholehearted obedience to the Guru's wisdom.
unverifiedDraft.teachingLocal: अहंकार का नाश निष्काम सेवा और गुरु-आज्ञा के पूर्ण समर्पण से ही संभव है।
unverifiedDraft.teachingPa: ਹਉਮੈ ਦਾ ਨਾਸ ਨਿਸ਼ਕਾਮ ਸੇਵਾ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੇ ਹੁਕਮ ਨੂੰ ਖਿੜੇ ਮੱਥੇ ਮੰਨਣ ਨਾਲ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
unverifiedDraft.moral: True surrender does not question or hesitate; it turns obedience into divine illumination.
unverifiedDraft.moralLocal: सच्चा शिष्य तर्क-वितर्क में समय नहीं गंवाता, बल्कि आज्ञापालन को तपस्या बना लेता है।
unverifiedDraft.moralPa: ਸੱਚਾ ਸਿੱਖ ਸ਼ੰਕੇ ਛੱਡ ਕੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੇ ਹੁਕਮ ਨੂੰ ਜੀਵਨ ਦਾ ਆਧਾਰ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
unverifiedDraft.legacy: Preserved and organized the divine hymns in Gurmukhi, enabling all castes to read scripture directly without priestly gatekeepers.
unverifiedDraft.legacyLocal: गुरुमुखी लिपि देकर जनसाधारण को धर्मग्रंथ पढ़ने और समझने का स्वाभिमान प्रदान किया।
unverifiedDraft.legacyPa: ਗੁਰਮੁਖੀ ਲਿਪੀ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ ਨੂੰ ਆਮ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਵਿੱਚ ਲਿਆਂਦਾ।

unverifiedDraft.tagline: The third Sikh Guru who instituted 'Pehle Pangat, Pache Sangat', abolished Sati and Purdah, and authored the immortal Anand Sahib.
unverifiedDraft.taglineLocal: तृतीय सिख गुरु जिन्होंने 'पहले पंगत, पाछे संगत' का नियम दिया, सती प्रथा मिटाई और आनंद साहिब की रचना की।
unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਤੀਜੇ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ 'ਪਹਿਲੇ ਪੰਗਤ ਪਾਛੇ ਸੰਗਤ' ਦਾ ਨਿਯਮ ਚਲਾਇਆ, ਸਤੀ ਪ੍ਰਥਾ ਦਾ ਖੰਡਨ ਕੀਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੰਦੁ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਕੀਤੀ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Finding his spiritual master in Guru Angad Dev Ji late in life, Amar Das spent twelve years carrying water from the river Beas every morning for the Guru's bath without ever turning his back. Becoming Guru at 73, he established Goindval Sahib, constructed the historic 84-step Baoli, and insisted that all visitors, including Emperor Akbar, sit and dine equally on the floor before spiritual audience.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: जीवन के उत्तरार्ध में गुरु अंगद देव जी से जुड़कर बारह वर्ष तक प्रतिदिन व्यास नदी से जल लाकर स्नान की सेवा की। ७३ वर्ष की आयु में गुरुपद संभालकर गोइन्दवाल साहिब बसाया, बाओली साहिब बनवाई और सम्राट अकबर को भी पंगत में बिठाकर लंगर छकाया।
unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਬਿਆਸ ਦਰਿਆ ਤੋਂ ਰੋਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਜਲ ਲਿਆ ਕੇ ਬਾਰਾਂ ਸਾਲ ਨਿਸ਼ਕਾਮ ਸੇਵਾ ਕੀਤੀ। ੭੩ ਸਾਲ ਦੀ ਉਮਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਗੁਰਗੱਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕੇ ਗੋਇੰਦਵਾਲ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਸਾਇਆ ਅਤੇ ਬਾਦਸ਼ਾਹ ਅਕਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਪੰਗਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਿਠਾ ਕੇ ਸਮਾਜਿਕ ਬਰਾਬਰੀ ਦਾ ਸੰਦੇਸ਼ ਦਿੱਤਾ।
unverifiedDraft.trial: When Guru Angad's son Datu kicked him out of jealousy, the elderly Guru massaged Datu's foot, asking forgiveness lest his old bones hurt him, retreating peacefully to Basarke.
unverifiedDraft.trialLocal: दातू द्वारा ईर्ष्यावश लात मारने पर भी क्रोध न कर उसके पैर सहलाते हुए क्षमा मांगना और शांति से एकांतवास चुनना उनकी विनम्रता की पराकाष्ठा थी।
unverifiedDraft.trialPa: ਦਾਤੂ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਲੱਤ ਮਾਰਨ 'ਤੇ ਵੀ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਨਾਲ ਉਸਦੇ ਪੈਰ ਘੁੱਟ ਕੇ ਖਿਮਾ ਮੰਗਣੀ ਅਤੇ ਵੈਰ-ਵਿਰੋਧ ਤੋਂ ਦੂਰ ਰਹਿਣਾ ਆਪ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਸਹਿਣਸ਼ੀਲਤਾ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਸੀ।
unverifiedDraft.teaching: Egalitarian fellowship dissolves social hierarchy; the nectar of bliss is found through inner poise and the Guru's Word.
unverifiedDraft.teachingLocal: समानता और सेवा से सामाजिक भेदभाव मिटता है; गुरु-शब्द में ही सच्चा आत्मिक आनंद निहित है।
unverifiedDraft.teachingPa: ਸਭ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਇੱਕ ਸਮਾਨ ਹਨ; ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ ਦੇ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜ ਕੇ ਹੀ ਸੱਚਾ ਆਤਮਿਕ ਅਨੰਦ ਮਿਲਦਾ ਹੈ।
unverifiedDraft.moral: Gentleness and supreme patience disarm wrath and establish lasting civilizational foundations.
unverifiedDraft.moralLocal: धैर्य और विनम्रता कठोरतम अहंकार को भी पिघला देते हैं।
unverifiedDraft.moralPa: ਧੀਰਜ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਨਾਲ ਵੱਡੇ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੇ ਕ੍ਰੋਧ ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਜਿੱਤਿਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
unverifiedDraft.legacy: Empowered women by condemning Sati and female infanticide, established the 22 Manjis missionary system, and created the pilgrimage center of Goindval.
unverifiedDraft.legacyLocal: सती व पर्दा प्रथा रोककर नारी को मान दिया और २२ मंजियों की संगठनात्मक व्यवस्था स्थापित की।
unverifiedDraft.legacyPa: ਇਸਤਰੀ ਜਾਤੀ ਦਾ ਮਾਣ ਬਹਾਲ ਕੀਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਿੱਖੀ ਪ੍ਰਚਾਰ ਲਈ ੨੨ ਮੰਜੀਆਂ ਸਥਾਪਿਤ ਕੀਤੀਆਂ।

unverifiedDraft.tagline: The fourth Sikh Guru who founded Amritsar, excavated the sacred Sarovar of Nectar, composed the Lavan wedding hymns, and personified limitless seva.
unverifiedDraft.taglineLocal: चतुर्थ सिख गुरु जिन्होंने अमृतसर की स्थापना की, अमृत सरोवर खुदवाया और विवाह के फेरों की 'लांवां' बाणी रची।
unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਚੌਥੇ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਵਸਾਇਆ, ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਸਰੋਵਰ ਦੀ ਖੁਦਾਈ ਕਰਵਾਈ ਅਤੇ ਆਨੰਦ ਕਾਰਜ ਦੀਆਂ 'ਲਾਵਾਂ' ਉਚਾਰਨ ਕੀਤੀਆਂ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Orphaned at a young age and selling boiled chickpeas (Ghunganiyan) in Lahore to survive, Bhai Jetha came to Goindval and threw himself into digging the Baoli. His selfless devotion caught Guru Amar Das's heart, who married his daughter Bibi Bhani to him. Sann 1574 CE, he was anointed the fourth Guru. Guru Ram Das purchased land and founded 'Guru ka Chakk' (later Ramdaspur / Amritsar), inviting merchants, artisans, and seekers of all 52 professions to settle there. He authored 679 hymns including the four sacred Lavan that unite human souls with the Divine in marriage.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: बचपन में अनाथ होकर उबले चने बेचकर निर्वाह करने वाले भाई जेठा जी गोइन्दवाल आकर बाओली निर्माण में जुट गए। उनकी निस्वार्थ सेवा से प्रसन्न होकर गुरु अमर दास जी ने अपनी पुत्री बीबी भानी का विवाह उनसे किया और बाद में गुरुगद्दी सौंपी। उन्होंने अमृतसर की नींव रखी, सरोवर की खुदाई शुरू करवाई और विवाह के चार पवित्र फेरों 'लांवां' की रचना की।
unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਬਚਪਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਯਤੀਮ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਘੁੰਗਣੀਆਂ ਵੇਚਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਭਾਈ ਜੇਠਾ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਗੋਇੰਦਵਾਲ ਆ ਕੇ ਬਾਉਲੀ ਦੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਕੀਤੀ। ਗੁਰੂ ਅਮਰ ਦਾਸ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਆਪ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਤੋਂ ਪ੍ਰਸੰਨ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਬੀਬੀ ਭਾਨੀ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਵਿਆਹ ਕੀਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਰਗੱਦੀ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ੀ। ਆਪ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਵਸਾਇਆ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੰਦ ਕਾਰਜ ਲਈ 'ਲਾਵਾਂ' ਦੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਰਚੀ।
unverifiedDraft.trial: Endured ridicule and insults from his wealthy relatives for doing manual earth-digging labor at Goindval, smiling with pure contentment and refusing to abandon humble service.
unverifiedDraft.trialLocal: धनी रिश्तेदारों द्वारा मिट्टी ढोने और मजदूरी करने पर ताने सुनने के बाद भी सेवा से विमुख न होना उनकी भक्ति की दृढ़ता थी।
unverifiedDraft.trialPa: ਸ਼ਰੀਕੇ-ਬਰਾਦਰੀ ਦੇ ਤਾਨਿਆਂ-ਮਿਹਣਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਪਰਵਾਹ ਕੀਤੇ ਬਿਨਾਂ ਗੋਇੰਦਵਾਲ ਵਿਖੇ ਮਿੱਟੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਟੋਕਰੀਆਂ ਢੋਣ ਦੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਨਿਰੰਤਰ ਨਿਭਾਈ।
unverifiedDraft.teaching: Rise in the ambrosial early hours, bathe in the pool of remembrance, and chant the Lord's Name with every breath.
unverifiedDraft.teachingLocal: अमृतवेले उठकर प्रभु के नाम में लीन होना और सेवा द्वारा अहंकार को शून्य करना ही जीवन का सत्य है।
unverifiedDraft.teachingPa: ਗੁਰ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਜੋ ਸਿਖੁ ਅਖਾਏ ਸੁ ਭਲਕੇ ਉਠਿ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਵੈ। ਨਾਮ ਜਪਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਨਾਲ ਸੇਵਾ ਕਰਨੀ ਹੀ ਸਿੱਖੀ ਦਾ ਮੂਲ ਹੈ।
unverifiedDraft.moral: Humble manual labor done with divine love elevates an orphan into the sovereign spiritual guide of humanity.
unverifiedDraft.moralLocal: निस्वार्थ श्रम और प्रेम से की गई सेवा मनुष्य को परमात्मा का स्वरूप बना देती है।
unverifiedDraft.moralPa: ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਸ਼ਕਾਮ ਸੇਵਾ ਨਾਲ ਕੀਤਾ ਨਿੱਕਾ ਜਿਹਾ ਕਾਰਜ ਵੀ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਨੂੰ ਆਤਮਿਕ ਬਾਦਸ਼ਾਹ ਬਣਾ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
unverifiedDraft.legacy: Founded Amritsar, the spiritual capital of the Sikhs, created the Lavan for sacred egalitarian marriage, and established the Masand system.
unverifiedDraft.legacyLocal: सिखों के आध्यात्मिक केंद्र अमृतसर की स्थापना की और विवाह के लिए चार लांवां की पवित्र मर्यादा स्थापित की।
unverifiedDraft.legacyPa: ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਵਸਾ ਕੇ ਸਿੱਖੀ ਦਾ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਸਥਾਪਿਤ ਕੀਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਆਨੰਦ ਕਾਰਜ ਦੀ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਮਰਯਾਦਾ ਕਾਇਮ ਕੀਤੀ।

unverifiedDraft.tagline: The sixth Sikh Guru who donned the twin swords of Miri and Piri, constructed the Akal Takht, and transformed seekers into Saint-Soldiers (Sant-Sipahis).
unverifiedDraft.taglineLocal: छठे सिख गुरु जिन्होंने मीरी और पीरी की दो तलवारें धारण कीं, अकाल तख्त का निर्माण किया और संतों को सिपाहियों में ढाला।
unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਛੇਵੇਂ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਮੀਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਪੀਰੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਦੋ ਤਲਵਾਰਾਂ ਪਹਿਨੀਆਂ, ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ ਤਖ਼ਤ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀ ਸਿਰਜਣਾ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਤ-ਸਿਪਾਹੀ ਬਣਾਇਆ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Following the supreme martyrdom of his father Guru Arjan Dev Ji on the burning sands of Lahore, eleven-year-old Hargobind was invested as Guru. He asked Baba Buddha Ji to gird him with two swords instead of the traditional seli: Miri (temporal sovereignty and defense of justice) and Piri (spiritual authority and inner truth). Directly opposite Sri Harmandir Sahib, he built the Akal Takht (Throne of the Timeless), holding court, receiving horses and weapons, and training a sovereign militia. Imprisoned by Jahangir in Gwalior Fort, he secured the unconditional release of 52 Hindu hill rajas alongside himself, earning the eternal title of 'Bandi Chhor' (Liberator of Captives). He fought four defensive battles against Mughal forces and emerged victorious in each, proving that righteousness must be defended with valor.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: पिता गुरु अर्जुन देव जी के बलिदान के उपरांत गद्दी संभालने पर ११ वर्ष की आयु में मीरी और पीरी की दो तलवारें धारण कीं। हरिमंदिर साहिब के समक्ष अकाल तख्त की स्थापना की और धर्मरक्षा के लिए सैन्य शक्ति संगठित की। ग्वालियर के किले में बंदी बनाए जाने पर उन्होंने अपने साथ ५२ हिंदू राजाओं को मुक्त करवाया और 'बंदी छोड़' कहलाए। मुगलों के साथ चार युद्ध लड़े और धर्म की विजय पताका फहराई।

unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਸੱਤਵੇਂ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ੨੨੦੦ ਘੋੜਸਵਾਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਫੌਜ ਰੱਖਦਿਆਂ ਵੀ ਅਥਾਹ ਰਹਿਮਤ ਤੇ ਦਇਆ ਦੀ ਮਿਸਾਲ ਕਾਇਮ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਦਾਰਾ ਸ਼ਿਕੋਹ ਲਈ ਦੁਰਲੱਭ ਦਵਾਈਆਂ ਭੇਜੀਆਂ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Grandson of Guru Hargobind, Har Rai possessed a heart of tender sensitivity. unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਅੱਠਵੇਂ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹ ਬਾਲਾ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ੫ ਸਾਲ ਦੀ ਉਮਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਗੁਰਗੱਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਲੀ, ਦਿੱਲੀ ਵਿਖੇ ਚੇਚਕ ਦੇ ਮਰੀਜ਼ਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਰਾ ਦੁੱਖ ਆਪਣੇ ਉੱਤੇ ਝੱਲ ਲਿਆ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Anointed Guru at the tender age of five, Guru Har Krishan possessed profound divine wisdom that astonished seasoned scholars. At Panjokhra near Ambala, when a proud Brahmin named Lal Chand challenged the child Guru to recite the Gita, Guru Har Krishan placed his stick upon an illiterate water-carrier named Chhaju, who immediately expounded the deepest philosophical verses of the Bhagavad Gita, humbling the scholar. Invited to Delhi by Raja Jai Singh, the Guru stayed at the Raja's Haveli (now Gurdwara Bangla Sahib). When an epidemic of smallpox and cholera ravaged Delhi, the child Guru walked fearlessly among the afflicted, comforting the dying, distributing clean water blessed with his touch, and establishing relief camps. He absorbed the epidemic onto his own physical body, leaving the mortal world at age seven with the final words 'Baba Bakale' pointing toward Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: पांच वर्ष की आयु में गुरुगद्दी संभालकर अपनी अलौकिक प्रज्ञा से सबको चकित किया। पंजोखरा में पंडित लाल चंद के अहंकार को मिटाने हेतु एक अनपढ़ झींवर छज्जू से गीता के गूढ़ रहस्यों की व्याख्या करवा दी। दिल्ली में राजा जयसिंह के भवन में ठहरकर हैजे व चेचक की महामारी के बीच दिन-रात पीड़ितों की सेवा की। अपने पावन स्पर्श से जल को अमृत बना दिया और अंततः रोगियों का कष्ट अपने शरीर पर लेकर मात्र सात वर्ष की आयु में 'बाबा बकाले' कहकर ज्योति-जोत समा गए।
unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਪੰਜ ਸਾਲ ਦੀ ਉਮਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਗੁਰਗੱਦੀ 'ਤੇ ਬਿਰਾਜਮਾਨ ਹੋਏ। ਪੰਜੋਖਰਾ ਵਿਖੇ ਪੰਡਿਤ ਲਾਲ ਚੰਦ ਦਾ ਹੰਕਾਰ ਤੋੜਨ ਲਈ ਛੱਜੂ ਝੀਵਰ ਦੇ ਸਿਰ 'ਤੇ ਛੜੀ ਰੱਖ ਕੇ ਉਸ ਪਾਸੋਂ ਗੀਤਾ ਦੇ ਅਰਥ ਕਰਵਾਏ। ਦਿੱਲੀ ਵਿਖੇ ਚੇਚਕ ਦੀ ਭਿਆਨਕ ਬਿਮਾਰੀ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਤਨ-ਮਨ ਨਾਲ ਸੇਵਾ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਚਰਨ-ਛੋਹ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤ ਜਲ ਨਾਲ ਹਜ਼ਾਰਾਂ ਰੋਗੀ ਠੀਕ ਕੀਤੇ। ਆਪ ਨੇ ਰੋਗ ਆਪਣੇ ਸਰੀਰ 'ਤੇ ਲੈ ਕੇ 'ਬਾਬਾ ਬਕਾਲੇ' ਆਖ ਕੇ ਜੋਤੀ-ਜੋਤਿ ਸਮਾ ਗਏ।

unverifiedDraft.tagline: The first of the Panj Pyare (Five Beloved Ones) who rose without hesitation when Guru Gobind Singh demanded a head at Anandpur Sahib on Vaisakhi 1699.
unverifiedDraft.taglineLocal: पंज प्यारों में प्रथम जिन्होंने वैशाखी १६९९ को आनंदपुर साहिब में गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी की तलवार के समक्ष सर्वप्रथम अपना शीश समर्पित किया।
unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਪੰਜਾਂ ਪਿਆਰਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਪਹਿਲੇ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ੧੬੯੯ ਦੀ ਵਿਸਾਖੀ ਨੂੰ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿਖੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਮੰਗ 'ਤੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਸੀਸ ਭੇਟ ਕੀਤਾ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Born as Daya Ram, a shopkeeper's son from Lahore, he journeyed to Anandpur Sahib seeking spiritual truth. On Vaisakhi day 1699, when Guru Gobind Singh emerged from a tent with a naked, blood-thirsting sword calling out, 'Is there any beloved Sikh ready to offer his head to my sword?', the assembly froze in terror. Daya Ram stepped forward unblinking, bowed his neck, and said, 'My head is yours, O Master.' After testing four more, the Guru brought them forth robed in saffron and royal splendor as the Panj Pyare, baptizing them with Khande di Pahul. Renamed Bhai Daya Singh, he became the leader of the Khalsa. He fought heroically at Anandpur and Chamkaur, and personally undertook the hazardous journey through hostile enemy terrain to deliver the Guru's fiery letter of defiance, the Zafarnama, directly into the hands of Emperor Aurangzeb in the Deccan.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: लाहौर के निवासी दया राम वैशाखी १६९९ को आनंदपुर साहिब की ऐतिहासिक सभा में उपस्थित थे। जब गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी ने नंगी तलवार लहराते हुए शीश की मांग की, तो पूरी सभा सन्न रह गई। भाई दया राम ने निर्भीक होकर अपना शीश अर्पित किया। अमृत छककर वे भाई दया सिंह बने। चमकौर की गढ़ी में वीरता से लड़े और बाद में औरंगजेब को दक्कन में गुरु जी का ऐतिहासिक विजय-पत्र 'ज़फ़रनामा' पहुंचाने का अत्यंत जोखिम भरा कार्य पूरा किया।
unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਲਾਹੌਰ ਦੇ ਦਇਆ ਰਾਮ ਨੇ ੧੬੯੯ ਦੀ ਵਿਸਾਖੀ ਨੂੰ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੇ ਸੀਸ ਮੰਗਣ 'ਤੇ ਬਿਨਾਂ ਝਿਜਕ ਆਪਣਾ ਸੀਸ ਭੇਟ ਕੀਤਾ। ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਛਕ ਕੇ ਭਾਈ ਦਇਆ ਸਿੰਘ ਬਣੇ ਅਤੇ ਪੰਜਾਂ ਪਿਆਰਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਪ੍ਰਮੁੱਖ ਅਸਥਾਨ ਪਾਇਆ। ਚਮਕੌਰ ਦੀ ਜੰਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਹਾਦਰੀ ਦਿਖਾਈ ਅਤੇ ਔਰੰਗਜ਼ੇਬ ਨੂੰ ਦੱਖਣ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦਾ 'ਜ਼ਫ਼ਰਨਾਮਾ' ਸੌਂਪਣ ਦੀ ਖ਼ਤਰਨਾਕ ਸੇਵਾ ਬਾਖ਼ੂਬੀ ਨਿਭਾਈ।
unverifiedDraft.trial: Stepping out from thousands of terrified spectators into the Guru's tent expecting imminent physical beheading.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born as Dharam Das, a Jat farmer from Hastinapur (near Meerut), he travelled to Anandpur Sahib thirsty for the nectar of divine truth. When Guru Gobind Singh demanded a second head after Bhai Daya Singh, Dharam Das stepped forward without a tremor of fear. Baptized as Bhai Dharam Singh, he stood as an immovable pillar of righteous duty. He fought alongside the Guru in the siege of Anandpur Sahib and through the bloody night of Chamkaur. Chosen as one of the three Sikhs commanded by the Panj Pyare to escort Guru Gobind Singh safely out of the encirclement of Chamkaur, he accompanied Bhai Daya Singh to deliver the Zafarnama to Aurangzeb, remaining at the Guru's side until Nanded.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: हस्तिनापुर के निवासी धर्म दास ने भाई दया सिंह के उपरांत दूसरा शीश अर्पित किया। अमृत छककर भाई धर्म सिंह बने। आनंदपुर साहिब की घेराबंदी और चमकौर के युद्ध में अदम्य साहस दिखाया। चमकौर की गढ़ी से पंज प्यारों के आदेशानुसार गुरु जी के साथ सुरक्षित निकलने वाले तीन सिंहों में वे शामिल थे।
unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਹਸਤਿਨਾਪੁਰ ਦੇ ਧਰਮ ਦਾਸ ਨੇ ਦੂਜੇ ਨੰਬਰ 'ਤੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੂੰ ਸੀਸ ਅਰਪਣ ਕੀਤਾ। ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਛਕ ਕੇ ਭਾਈ ਧਰਮ ਸਿੰਘ ਅਖਵਾਏ। ਚਮਕੌਰ ਦੀ ਗੜ੍ਹੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਡਟ ਕੇ ਮੁਕਾਬਲਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਪੰਜਾਂ ਪਿਆਰਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਹੁਕਮ ਤਹਿਤ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੂੰ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਅਤ ਬਾਹਰ ਲਿਆਉਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਰਹੇ।
unverifiedDraft.trial: Standing up before thousands to offer his head immediately after witnessing a bloodied sword emerge from the tent.
unverifiedDraft.trialLocal: तंबू से रक्तरंजित तलवार बाहर आने के बाद भी दूसरे शीश के लिए बिना झिझक आगे बढ़ना उनकी निष्ठा की पराकाष्ठा थी।
unverifiedDraft.trialPa: ਖ਼ੂਨ ਨਾਲ ਲਿਬੜੀ ਤਲਵਾਰ ਦੇਖਣ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਵੀ ਸੀਸ ਭੇਟ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਅੱਗੇ ਵਧਣਾ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਦਲੇਰੀ ਦਾ ਸਬੂਤ ਸੀ।

unverifiedDraft.moral: When righteousness is woven into your soul, sacrifice becomes as natural as breathing.

unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਪੰਜਾਂ ਪਿਆਰਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਤੀਜੇ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੋ ਜਗਨਨਾਥ ਪੁਰੀ ਤੋਂ ਆਏ, ਸੀਸ ਭੇਟ ਕੀਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਚਮਕੌਰ ਦੀ ਜੰਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ਼ਹਾਦਤ ਦਾ ਜਾਮ ਪੀਤਾ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Born as Himmat Rai in Puri, Odisha, he belonged to the water-carrier (Jhir) community, marginalized by rigid caste systems. Hearing the universal glory of Guru Gobind Singh's court, he travelled across the subcontinent to Anandpur Sahib. On Vaisakhi 1699, when the Guru called for a third head, Himmat Rai arose without hesitation. The Guru baptized him as Bhai Himmat Singh, obliterating all stigma of caste and birth, declaring him a prince of the Khalsa. In December 1705, inside the mud fortress of Chamkaur, surrounded by a Mughal army numbering in hundreds of thousands, Bhai Himmat Singh led a small sally out of the gates, cutting through waves of enemy troops before embracing glorious martyrdom.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: जगन्नाथ पुरी के जल-वाहक परिवार में जन्मे हिम्मत राय जाति-पाति के बंधनों को तोड़कर आनंदपुर साहिब पहुंचे। वैशाखी १६९९ को तीसरा शीश अर्पित कर भाई हिम्मत सिंह बने। चमकौर की गढ़ी में मात्र ४० सिंहों के साथ लाखों की मुगल सेना का सामना करते हुए अद्वितीय पराक्रम दिखाया और वीरगति प्राप्त की।
unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਜਗਨਨਾਥ ਪੁਰੀ ਦੇ ਰਹਿਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਹਿੰਮਤ ਰਾਇ ਨੇ ਜਾਤ-ਪਾਤ ਦੇ ਭੇਦਭਾਵ ਮਿਟਾ ਕੇ ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿਖੇ ਤੀਜਾ ਸੀਸ ਭੇਟ ਕੀਤਾ। ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੇ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਛਕਾ ਕੇ ਭਾਈ ਹਿੰਮਤ ਸਿੰਘ ਬਣਾਇਆ। ਚਮਕੌਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀ ਅਸਾਵੀਂ ਜੰਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੁਗ਼ਲ ਫ਼ੌਜਾਂ ਦੇ ਆਹੂ ਲਾਹੁੰਦਿਆਂ ਸ਼ਹੀਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤ ਕੀਤੀ।

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born as Mohkam Chand in the coastal sacred city of Dwarka, Gujarat, he was a calico-printer/tailor (Chhimba). Drawn to the spiritual light of Anandpur Sahib, he undertook the immense pilgrimage to Punjab. On Vaisakhi 1699, as the Guru called out for a fourth sacrifice, Mohkam Chand stood tall, folding his hands and bowing his head to the sword. Blessed with Amrit, he was reborn as Bhai Mohkam Singh, a sovereign lion of the Khalsa. He mastered archery and swordsmanship, serving the Guru through numerous skirmishes with hill rajas and imperial forces. In the epic defense of Chamkaur fortress in 1705, he stepped onto the battlefield with a small jatha, fighting with superhuman bravery until he fell heroically on the blood-soaked field.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born as Sahib Chand in Bidar (Karnataka), where Guru Nanak Dev Ji had historically released a spring of sweet water (Guru Nanak Jhira), he belonged to the barber (Nai) community. Yearning for spiritual liberation, he walked thousands of miles to Anandpur Sahib. On Vaisakhi 1699, when the Guru made his fifth and final call for a head, Sahib Chand walked up with unshakeable serenity, completing the Panj Pyare. Anointed with Amrit as Bhai Sahib Singh, he was transformed into a master of the double-edged sword. He fought relentlessly against hill chieftains and Mughal oppressors. At Chamkaur Sahib in 1705, Bhai Sahib Singh charged into the vast enemy lines alongside Bhai Himmat Singh and Bhai Mohkam Singh, displaying legendary valor until his glorious last breath.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Eldest son of Guru Gobind Singh Ji, Sahibzada Ajit Singh was trained from infancy in equestrian warfare, archery, swordsmanship, and sacred scripture. At the age of twelve, he successfully led a rescue detachment to retrieve a poor Brahmin's bride who had been abducted by the Mughal chieftain of Bassi Pathanan, restoring her honor without taking a single coin. During the bitter siege of Anandpur Sahib, he fought relentlessly. In December 1705, inside the besieged mud haveli of Chamkaur, with only forty Sikhs resisting an imperial horde of hundreds of thousands, eighteen-year-old Ajit Singh bowed before his father and begged permission to enter the battlefield. Guru Gobind Singh personally buckled armor onto his youth, crowned him with a plume, and sent him forth. Ajit Singh charged with seven warriors, shattering enemy ranks until his spear snapped, drawing his sword and fighting until his last breath.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born at Anandpur Sahib, Sahibzada Jujhar Singh was named 'Jujhar' (the resolute warrior). At age fourteen, he found himself inside the mud fortress of Chamkaur beside his father. He watched from the ramparts as his elder brother Ajit Singh fought like a lion and fell embraced by the earth. Rather than trembling, Jujhar Singh approached Guru Gobind Singh and said, 'Father, permit me to go where my brother has gone. I will not dishonor your blood.' When Sikhs protested that he was only a child, the Guru replied, 'All forty here are my children. He is a soldier of the Akal Purakh.' Guru Gobind Singh kissed his forehead and dispatched him with five Sikhs. Jujhar Singh fought with astonishing ferocity, splitting enemy lines until an overwhelming barrage felled the heroic youth.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Separated from his father and elder brothers during the crossing of the stormy Sarsa river, nine-year-old Zorawar Singh and his seven-year-old brother Fateh Singh were accompanied by their grandmother Mata Gujri Ji. Betrayed by their servant Gangu, they were captured and imprisoned in the freezing cold open tower (Thanda Burj) of Sirhind in the dead of winter. Hauled before Nawab Wazir Khan's court, the child prince entered with his head held high, roaring 'Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh!'. Bribed with royal palaces, wealth, and princely status if he converted to Islam, Zorawar Singh spat upon the offers. Threatened with excruciating torture, he declared that the sons of Guru Gobind Singh bow only to the Timeless Creator. In December 1705, the tyrant ordered the two innocent children bricked alive into a brick wall.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Youngest of the four Sahibzadas, Baba Fateh Singh was barely seven years old when the imperial siege of Anandpur Sahib forced the evacuation. In the biting frost of December, separated from his parents, he was kept without warm clothing in the open Thanda Burj. Before the court of Wazir Khan, when courtiers mocked him that his father and brothers were dead and urged him to bow, seven-year-old Fateh Singh stood shoulder to shoulder with Zorawar Singh and proclaimed that death holds no terror for a son of the tenth Master. When the executioners built the brick wall around them, the children chanted sacred hymns. When the wall collapsed, the tyrant had their throats slit, securing their immortal victory (Fateh).

unverifiedDraft.journey: Mata Tripta was a woman of profound inner piety, gentleness, and silent devotion in Talwandi. When her divine child Nanak was born in 1469 CE, she perceived from the very first hour that this was no ordinary mortal. While her husband Mehta Kalu often grew frustrated with Nanak's disinterest in worldly commerce, farming, and cattle-grazing, Mata Tripta was the protective sanctuary who comforted her son, understanding that his mind was anchored in the Divine. She supported his radical charity during the Sacha Sauda (True Bargain) when he fed hungry dervishes instead of doing business. When Guru Nanak set out on his four long Udasis (spiritual odysseys across Asia), she endured the painful ache of separation with immense prayer and quiet grace, rejoicing when he returned to establish Kartarpur Sahib.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Five years elder to Guru Nanak, Bebe Nanaki shared an unshakeable soul-bond with her brother. While the village gossiped that Nanak was idle or mad, Nanaki saw with radiant clarity that the light of the Creator shone through him. When she married Jai Ram and moved to Sultanpur Lodhi, she invited Nanak to join them, securing him employment at Nawab Daulat Khan Lodhi's royal granary (Modikhana). At Sultanpur Lodhi, when Nanak gave away grains counting 'Tera, Tera' (Thine, Thine), she stood by him unconditionally. Understanding that divine poetry required musical wings, she purchased and gifted a Rebab (stringed instrument) to Bhai Mardana, initiating the immortal tradition of Kirtan. She is recognized in Sikh history as the very first Sikh.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Wife of the second Guru, Guru Angad Dev Ji, Mata Khivi was the beating heart of the community at Khadur Sahib. Long before modern social welfare existed, she personally organized and oversaw the preparation and distribution of Guru ka Langar. She ensured that the food was not merely surviving gruel, but rich, nutritious, and served with unconditional love. Her signature dish was 'Kheer' (rice pudding cooked in rich milk and ghee), which she served with her own hands to kings, beggars, outcasts, and ascetics sitting together as equals. Her maternal warmth and administrative genius sustained the fledgling Sikh community during harsh times. She lived through the Guruships of Guru Angad, Guru Amar Das, Guru Ram Das, and saw young Guru Arjan Dev, remaining an anchor of wisdom until age 75.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Daughter of the third Guru, Mata Bhani was steeped in prayer and service from childhood. When her father was aging, she attended to his daily bath with extraordinary vigilance. Once, when a leg of the Guru's wooden bath-stool broke, she thrust her own hand beneath the broken peg to prevent the elderly Guru from falling, holding the immense weight while the splintered wood pierced deep into her palm and blood flowed. When Guru Amar Das finished and saw the pool of blood, he blessed her devotion. Married to Bhai Jetha (Guru Ram Das), she lived in utter simplicity, digging earth for the sacred sarovars. As mother to Guru Arjan Dev Ji, she imparted the highest spiritual fortitude that prepared him to face burning martyrdom with absolute peace.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Consort of the fifth Guru, Mata Ganga was a woman of noble dignity and gentle demeanor. When relatives taunted her for being childless, Guru Arjan Dev advised her to seek the blessing of the venerable saint Baba Buddha Ji. Initially travelling in royal palanquins with an ostentatious entourage, Baba Buddha felt embarrassed and did not bless her. Realizing her mistake, Mata Ganga cast aside royal luxury, ground fresh corn with her own hands, baked rustic Missi rotis, prepared raw onions and freshly churned butter, and walked barefoot like a humble village woman to Baba Buddha's forest abode. Delighted by her pure humility, Baba Buddha crushed an onion with his fist and prophesied: 'As I crush this onion, so will your son crush the heads of tyrants!' She gave birth to Guru Hargobind. Later, when Guru Arjan Dev attained martyrdom, Mata Ganga bore the supreme loss with tranquil resignation to the divine Will, guiding the young Guru.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Consort of the tenth Master, Mata Sundari was a woman of towering intellect, administrative brilliance, and profound spiritual grounding. After the evacuation of Anandpur Sahib and the martyrdom of her four sons, she joined Guru Gobind Singh at Talwandi Sabo. Following the Guru's ascension at Nanded in 1708, she resided at Delhi (Gurdwara Mata Sundari). For nearly forty years, during the darkest period of Mughal persecution when bounties were put on Sikh heads, Mata Sundari acted as the supreme supreme guiding matriarch of the Khalsa. She issued Hukamnamas (edicts) to Sikh sangats across India, mediated intense internal disputes between the Tat Khalsa and Bandai Khalsa to preserve unity, commissioned Bhai Mani Singh to collect and codify the writings of Guru Gobind Singh into the Dasam Granth, and preserved the historical institutions of the faith.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born in Rohtas (now Pakistan), Sahib Devan dedicated her heart exclusively to the tenth Guru. When her father brought her to Anandpur Sahib, Guru Gobind Singh explained that he had taken a vow of worldly celibacy, but accepted her spiritual surrender. On Vaisakhi day 1699, when the Guru was preparing the Khande di Pahul (immortal nectar) with iron and double-edged sword, Mata Sahib Devan approached and dropped sugar puffs (Patashas) into the iron cauldron. The Guru smiled and proclaimed: 'You have perfected the Amrit; now my Khalsa shall not only possess the warrior's iron courage, but also the sweetness of boundless compassion!' The Guru bestowed upon her the eternal spiritual motherhood of the entire Khalsa nation: every baptized Sikh declares to this day that their spiritual father is Guru Gobind Singh and their mother is Mata Sahib Kaur.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Resident of the village of Chamkaur, Bibi Sharan Kaur was a devout Sikh woman who heard the earth-shattering clash of arms in December 1705. When the battle subsided and Guru Gobind Singh departed under Panj Pyare orders, thousands of Mughal and hill troops occupied the area, having strictly forbidden the cremation of the fallen Sikh martyrs to desecrate their remains. Sharan Kaur could not bear the thought of the bodies of Sahibzada Ajit Singh, Jujhar Singh, and the brave Sikhs being left to scavengers. In the freezing dead of night, slipping like a shadow past imperial sentries, she crawled through the gore-soaked field. One by one, she gathered the bodies, assembled a pyre of wood, and lit the fire. When the flames alerted Mughal soldiers, they surrounded her. Refusing capture or dishonor, she leaped into the sacred funeral flames, achieving immortal martyrdom.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born into a distinguished Chhibber Brahmin family of Karyala, Bhai Mati Das was the Diwan (chief administrator) of Guru Tegh Bahadur's court. When Kashmiri Pandits pleaded for salvation against forced conversions by Aurangzeb, Guru Tegh Bahadur resolved to lay down his life. Bhai Mati Das, along with his brother Bhai Sati Das and Bhai Dayala, accompanied the Guru to Delhi. Imprisoned in Kotwali at Chandni Chowk, Aurangzeb's qazis offered Mati Das wealth, royal governorship, and beautiful maidens if he embraced Islam. When he spit on the offers, they threatened him with the most horrific execution. Bound tightly between two vertical wooden posts, executioners placed a jagged iron saw on the crown of his skull. As the saw cut through his flesh, bone, and brain, Bhai Mati Das did not utter a single cry of agony; his lips moved continuously in unbroken recitation of Japji Sahib until his body fell in two equal halves.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Younger brother of Bhai Mati Das, Bhai Sati Das was a gifted scholar of Persian, Sanskrit, and Gurmukhi who served as the chief Persian scribe and secretary to Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. He recorded the Guru's holy travels, teachings, and administrative letters. Standing alongside his Master and elder brother in Delhi's Kotwali, he refused all imperial bribes of rank and safety. Immediately after witnessing Bhai Mati Das sawn in two and Bhai Dayala boiled alive, the executioners turned to Sati Das, demanding that he accept Islam or face a fiery death. Sati Das calmly replied that fire can burn only the temporary garments of clay, not the immortal soul anchored in the Guru. Bound to a wooden stake, executioners wrapped his entire body in thick rolls of cotton wool, poured oil over him, and set it ablaze. Sati Das stood like an effulgent beacon of divine light, chanting hymns until his breath dissolved into the Timeless.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Bhai Dayala (also known as Bhai Dial Das) was the younger brother of Bhai Mani Singh and head of the Guru's household affairs. Dedicated to Guru Tegh Bahadur from his early youth, he was entrusted with managing the pilgrimage tour across eastern India to Assam. When the Guru resolved to defend the fundamental human right to freedom of conscience, Bhai Dayala insisted on accompanying him to Delhi. Following the brutal martyrdom of Bhai Mati Das, the Mughal qazis dragged Bhai Dayala to the center of Chandni Chowk. A massive copper cauldron (Deg) filled with water was set atop roaring firewood until the water bubbled violently. They demanded he abandon Sikhi or be immersed in boiling liquid. Bhai Dayala looked at the cauldron with serene joy, bowed in the direction of Guru Tegh Bahadur, and climbed into the scalding water. As the boiling liquid tore his skin and boiled his flesh, he sat cross-legged with folded hands, his voice resounding with the sacred words of Japji Sahib until his soul merged into the eternal Light.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: भाई दयाला जी (भाई दयाल दास) भाई मनी सिंह के भ्राता थे और गुरु तेग बहादुर जी के अत्यंत विश्वासपात्र सेवक थे। गुरु जी के साथ दिल्ली पहुंचकर उन्होंने मुगलों की हर यातना को हँसते-हँसते झेला। भाई मती दास के बलिदान के बाद काजियों ने उन्हें खौलते हुए पानी के बड़े कड़ाह में डालने की धमकी दी। धर्म न छोड़ने पर उन्हें उबलते हुए देग में बैठा दिया गया। उबलते जल में भी वे पद्मासन लगाकर हाथ जोड़कर बैठे रहे और जपजी साहिब का पाठ करते हुए अपने प्राण त्याग दिए।

unverifiedDraft.tagline: The saintly disciple of Guru Gobind Singh who carried a goatskin water-bag (Mashak) onto the battlefield to serve water to wounded soldiers, both Sikh and Mughal, seeing only the Guru in all.

unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਉਹ ਅਨੋਖੇ ਸਿੱਖ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਜੰਗ ਦੇ ਮੈਦਾਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਿਨਾਂ ਵੈਰ-ਵਿਰੋਧ ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਤੇ ਮੁਗ਼ਲਾਂ ਦੋਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਣੀ ਪਿਲਾ ਕੇ 'ਨਾ ਕੋ ਬੈਰੀ ਨਹੀ ਬਿਗਾਨਾ' ਦਾ ਸੰਦੇਸ਼ ਦਿੱਤਾ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Born into a wealthy merchant family in Sodhra, Kanhaiya renounced material wealth in search of true peace, eventually finding his spiritual master in Guru Tegh Bahadur and later Guru Gobind Singh. During the fierce battles at Anandpur Sahib, he took up the service of carrying a leather mashak (water-skin), walking between dying men on the gory battlefield. Some Sikhs noticed with outrage that Kanhaiya was reviving fallen enemy soldiers—pouring cooling water down the throats of Mughal and hill troops who had just fired arrows at the Sikhs. They dragged him before Guru Gobind Singh, accusing him of treason. The Guru asked him, 'Kanhaiya, is it true that you have been giving water to the enemy?' Kanhaiya replied with celestial simplicity: 'Master, since you opened my inner eye, I see no enemy and no stranger on that battlefield. I see only your radiant face in every wounded, dying soul.' Overcome with divine joy, Guru Gobind Singh embraced him, handed him a box of medicinal ointment, and said, 'Go, Kanhaiya! From now on, not only give them water, but also dress their wounds!'
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: सोदरा के धनी परिवार के कन्हैया जी गुरु चरणों में समर्पित होकर आनंदपुर साहिब में सेवा करने लगे। आनंदपुर के भीषण युद्ध में वे मशक लेकर रणभूमि में घायलों को जल पिलाने लगे। कुछ सिखों ने देखा कि वे मुगल सैनिकों को भी जल पिला रहे हैं। उन्होंने गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी से शिकायत की। जब गुरु जी ने पूछा, तो कन्हैया जी ने कहा, 'महाराज! रणभूमि में मुझे न कोई सिख दिखता है न कोई मुगल; मुझे तो हर घायल में केवल आपका ही मुखड़ा दिखाई देता है।' गुरु जी ने गदगद होकर उन्हें गले से लगा लिया और मरहम की डिब्बी देते हुए कहा कि आज से जल के साथ घावों पर मरहम भी लगाओ।
unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਸੋਦਰਾ ਦੇ ਰਹਿਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਭਾਈ ਘਨ੍ਹਈਆ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀ ਜੰਗ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਮਸ਼ਕ ਚੁੱਕ ਕੇ ਮੈਦਾਨ-ਏ-ਜੰਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਜ਼ਖ਼ਮੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਣੀ ਪਿਲਾਉਣ ਦੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਸੰਭਾਲੀ। ਕੁਝ ਸਿੰਘਾਂ ਨੇ ਸ਼ਿਕਾਇਤ ਕੀਤੀ ਕਿ ਇਹ ਦੁਸ਼ਮਣ ਮੁਗ਼ਲਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਪਾਣੀ ਪਿਲਾਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਪੁੱਛੇ ਜਾਣ 'ਤੇ ਆਪ ਨੇ ਹੱਥ ਜੋੜ ਕੇ ਕਿਹਾ, 'ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹ! ਮੈਨੂੰ ਤਾਂ ਕੋਈ ਵੈਰੀ ਜਾਂ ਬੇਗਾਨਾ ਦਿਸਦਾ ਹੀ ਨਹੀਂ, ਹਰ ਚਿਹਰੇ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਤੁਹਾਡਾ ਹੀ ਨੂਰ ਝਲਕਦਾ ਹੈ।' ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੇ ਖ਼ੁਸ਼ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਛਾਤੀ ਨਾਲ ਲਾਇਆ ਅਤੇ ਮਰਹਮ ਦੀ ਡੱਬੀ ਦੇ ਕੇ ਜ਼ਖ਼ਮਾਂ ਦੀ ਪੱਟੀ ਕਰਨ ਦਾ ਹੁਕਮ ਦਿੱਤਾ।

unverifiedDraft.tagline: The legendary warrior who, armed with the serpent-spear Nagni Barchha, charged solo on horseback and pierced the armored war elephant at the battle of Lohgarh.

unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀ ਜੰਗ ਵਿੱਚ 'ਨਾਗਣੀ ਬਰਛੇ' ਨਾਲ ਲੋਹਗੜ੍ਹ ਦੇ ਕਿਲ੍ਹੇ ਦਾ ਬੂਹਾ ਤੋੜਨ ਆਏ ਮਸਤ ਹਾਥੀ ਦੇ ਮੱਥੇ ਨੂੰ ਵਿੰਨ੍ਹਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਅਣਖੀਲੇ ਯੋਧੇ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Son of Bhai Mani Singh, Bhai Bachittar Singh was raised in the martial discipline of the Guru's court. In 1700 CE, during the siege of Lohgarh fort at Anandpur Sahib, the allied hill rajas and imperial forces grew desperate. Raja Kesari Chand brought forward a colossal male war-elephant, heavily intoxicated with liquor and encased in thick steel armor with double-edged curved blades strapped to its tusks, to shatter the fort gates. When Sikhs whispered about the beast, Guru Gobind Singh looked at the lean, wiry Bachittar Singh and commanded him to face the elephant. Handing him the sacred serpent-spear (Nagni Barchha), the Guru blessed him. Bachittar Singh rode out on his stallion, stood in his stirrups as the roaring monster charged, and drove the spear with superhuman velocity straight through the steel forehead-plate of the beast into its brain. Maddened with agony, the elephant turned around and trampled hundreds of enemy soldiers, turning the tide of battle in minutes.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: भाई मनी सिंह के सुपुत्र भाई बचित्र सिंह आनंदपुर साहिब के कुशल योद्धा थे। १७०० में जब पहाड़ी राजाओं ने लोहगढ़ किले के फाटक तोड़ने के लिए शराब पिलाए और लोहे के बख्तर से ढके मतवाले हाथी को आगे किया, तो गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी ने दुबले-पतले बचित्र सिंह को उस हाथी का सामना करने का आदेश दिया। गुरु जी ने उन्हें 'नागणी बरछा' सौंपा। बचित्र सिंह ने अपने घोड़े को दौड़ाकर उछलते हुए बरछे से हाथी के लोहे के बख्तर को भेदते हुए उसके मस्तक को चीर दिया। घायल हाथी पीछे भागा और अपनी ही सेना को रौंद डाला।

unverifiedDraft.journey: Another illustrious son of Bhai Mani Singh, Bhai Uday Singh was a commanding figure of strength, tactical daring, and absolute devotion. During the battle of Taragarh at Anandpur Sahib, Raja Kesari Chand of Jaswal bragged arrogantly that he would bring Guru Gobind Singh's head or never return. Guru Gobind Singh appointed Uday Singh to counter him. Riding into the fray, Uday Singh matched Kesari Chand blade for blade, severed the raja's head with a lightning stroke of his scimitar, impaled the head upon his spear, and brought it back into the Guru's presence, breaking the morale of the hill armies. Five years later, during the harrowing evacuation of Anandpur in the dead of winter 1705, Uday Singh commanded the rear guard of just fifty Sikhs at Shahi Tibbi. Ordered to hold off hundreds of thousands of pursuing imperial troops until the Guru crossed the flooded Sarsa river, Uday Singh fought like a titan until every single warrior fell in glorious defense of their Master.

unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਚਾਂਦਨੀ ਚੌਕ ਦਿੱਲੀ ਤੋਂ ਨੌਵੇਂ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹ ਦਾ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਸੀਸ ਮੁਗ਼ਲ ਪਹਿਰੇ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਚੁੱਕ ਕੇ ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਪਹੁੰਚਾਉਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਮਹਾਨ ਯੋਧੇ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ 'ਰੰਘਰੇਟਾ ਗੁਰੂ ਕਾ ਬੇਟਾ' ਦਾ ਖ਼ਿਤਾਬ ਮਿਲਿਆ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Born into a marginalized Mazhabi (Ranghreta) family in Delhi, Bhai Jaita was deeply devoted to Guru Tegh Bahadur. On that fateful November day in 1675 at Chandni Chowk, after the Guru was publicly beheaded, imperial criers announced that anyone daring to touch the body would be flayed alive. As a freak dust storm swept over the city, Bhai Jaita courageously slipped through the terror-stricken crowd, wrapped the sacred severed head of Guru Tegh Bahadur in pristine cloth, and carried it with him. Walking day and night across 350 kilometers through police checkpoints, he reached Kiratpur Sahib and presented the sacred head to young Guru Gobind Singh. The nine-year-old Guru embraced Jaita passionately, weeping with love, and conferred upon him and his community the eternal blessing: 'Ranghreta Guru Ka Beta' (The Ranghreta is the Guru's own son!). Bhai Jaita took Amrit to become Bhai Jiwan Singh, commanded troops, trained the young Sahibzadas, authored Sri Gurkatha, and fell fighting heroically at Chamkaur in 1705.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Son of Bhai Subeg Singh, young Shahbaz Singh studied Arabic and Persian under a Muslim Kazi in Lahore. Gifted with extraordinary intellect, exceptional handsome looks, and sharp debate skills, his teacher sought to convert him to Islam. Shahbaz refused, defending the universal wisdom of Guru Nanak with impeccable theological clarity. Enraged, the Kazi lodged false blasphemy charges against the boy. unverifiedDraft.journey: Born in Khemkaran, Gurbaksh Singh was baptized by Bhai Mani Singh and became a revered Nihang warrior-saint in the Taruna Dal. In December 1764, the Afghan invader Ahmad Shah Abdali swept into Punjab on his seventh invasion, specifically intending to demolish Sri Harmandir Sahib once again. Aware that the main Dal Khalsa forces had temporarily retreated to the Lakhi jungle for guerrilla tactics, Baba Gurbaksh Singh refused to leave the Golden Temple defenceless. He and twenty-nine elderly and young Sikhs dressed themselves in ceremonial saffron wedding robes, performing their own Ardas of martyrdom. unverifiedDraft.journey: Head of the Karor Singhia Misl, Sardar Baghel Singh was one of the brilliant military strategists of eighteenth-century India. In March 1783, commanding a united Sikh confederacy army of thirty thousand warriors (the Dal Khalsa), Baghel Singh swept past Mughal defenses and captured the imperial capital of Delhi. His forces stormed the Red Fort and hoisted the Sikh Nishan Sahib upon the Diwan-i-Aam. Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II sued for peace, conceding the Sikhs' terms: Baghel Singh was granted the right to collect 37.5% (six annas in a rupee) of all octroi duties of Delhi and received imperial authority to locate and construct shrines at all historical sites associated with the Sikh Gurus. With remarkable diligence, Baghel Singh spent months in Delhi identifying the sacred sites, constructing Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib (site of Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom), Gurdwara Bangla Sahib, Gurdwara Rakab Ganj, Gurdwara Bala Sahib, Gurdwara Majnu ka Tilla, and Gurdwara Moti Bagh.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Grandson of Hardas Singh who fought under Guru Gobind Singh, Jassa Singh was a carpenter-artisan by birth and a military genius by calling. When Amritsar was under siege in 1748, he fortified the small mud fortress of Ram Rauni, from which his misl took the name 'Ramgarhia'. A brilliant military engineer and fierce warrior, he built fortifications across the Doaba and Majha regions. In the 1783 capture of Delhi alongside Jassa Singh Ahluwalia and Baghel Singh, Ramgarhia troops stormed the Red Fort. From the Diwan-i-Khas, Jassa Singh personally detached the enormous marble coronation slab on which Mughal emperors had been crowned, hitched it to elephants, and hauled it across four hundred miles back to Sri Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar. Today, that very Mughal coronation stone lies subjugated beneath the feet of visitors inside the Ramgarhia Bunga, testament to the fall of imperial tyranny.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born into a Virk Jat family of Faizullapur, Kapur Singh took Amrit at the 1721 Amritsar gathering. During the brutal persecution by Zakariya Khan when Sikhs lived in the wilderness, Kapur Singh emerged as their beloved field commander. In 1733, the Mughal court, desperate for truce, sent a robe of honor, a jagir, and the title of 'Nawab' to the Sikhs. The assembled Khalsa refused the title, considering it beneath the sovereignty bestowed by Guru Gobind Singh. When urged to accept for political breathing room, the Khalsa threw the robe at the feet of Kapur Singh, who was humbly fanning the horses and the Sangat in the Langar. Kapur Singh accepted the title only after touching it to the feet of five beloved Sikhs, stipulating that he would never abandon his humble chore of waving the fan (pankha) for the Sangat. In 1734, he brilliantly reorganized the entire Sikh martial force into the Budha Dal (veterans overseeing gurdwaras and spiritual discipline) and Taruna Dal (youth fighters defending the borders), laying the bedrock of the 12 Sikh Misls.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Grandson of Sardar Gaur Singh of Attari, Sham Singh was one of Maharaja Ranjit Singh's most respected and courageous commanders. In February 1846, during the First Anglo-Sikh War at the battle of Sabraon, the traitorous prime minister Lal Singh and commander Tej Singh fled the field, intentionally destroying the pontoon bridge over the Sutlej to trap their own army. Sham Singh, disgusted by the betrayal, vowed before Sri Guru Granth Sahib that he would never return to Attari alive in defeat. He dressed himself in pure white robes (the bridal attire of martyrdom), mounted his favorite white steed, and rallied the abandoned Khalsa soldiers. Sword raised high, eyes burning with sovereign pride, he charged headlong into the teeth of the 53rd British Regiment and heavy grape-shot artillery. Struck by seven musket balls, he fell embracing the earth with his face toward the enemy.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Once a notorious robber in his youth, Bidhi Chand was spiritually awakened by Bhai Adli and surrendered his life to Guru Arjan Dev and Guru Hargobind. Transformed into an exemplary saint-soldier, he combined spiritual devotion with unmatched cunning and agility. When the Mughal governor confiscated two magnificent horses (Dilbagh and Gulbagh) gifted to Guru Hargobind by Kabul Sikhs and locked them inside Lahore Fort, Bidhi Chand undertook to retrieve them. He entered the fort disguised first as a grass-cutter, cutting pristine grass and winning the keeper's trust. Unlocking Dilbagh at midnight, he rode him to the battlements, leaped the horse into the raging river Ravi beneath, and escaped. Returning weeks later disguised as an astrologer, he deduced how the first horse had vanished, mounted Gulbagh, proclaimed his identity aloud, and leaped into the river once again, returning both horses to the Guru.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born into a Mirasi Muslim family in Rai Bhoi di Talwandi, Mardana was nine years elder to Nanak. From youth, their souls were intertwined. When Guru Nanak received divine revelation and composed sacred poetry, it was Mardana's fingers dancing across the strings of his Rebab that gave melody to the Guru's words. For over thirty years, through freezing Himalayan heights, scorching Arabian deserts, dense jungles of Assam, and the holy cities of Mecca, Medina, Baghdad, and Banaras, Mardana walked stride for stride beside Guru Nanak. Whenever divine revelation descended, the Guru would say, 'Mardana, play the rebab, the divine Word has arrived!' (Mardania, rabab chhed, bani aayi hai!). Mardana authored three sacred hymns preserved inside Sri Guru Granth Sahib under Rag Bihagara, standing as an eternal bridge of interfaith harmony.

unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਤਲਵੰਡੀ ਦੇ ਭਾਈ ਮਰਦਾਨਾ ਜੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਬਚਪਨ ਦੇ ਮਿੱਤਰ ਸਨ। ਜਦੋਂ ਵੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ 'ਤੇ ਇਲਾਹੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਉਤਰਦੀ, ਤਾਂ ਆਪ ਫ਼ੁਰਮਾਉਂਦੇ, 'ਮਰਦਾਨਿਆਂ! ਰਬਾਬ ਛੇੜ, ਬਾਣੀ ਆਈ ਐ।' ਆਪ ਨੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨਾਲ ਚਹੁੰ ਉਦਾਸੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੱਕਾ, ਮਦੀਨਾ, ਬਗ਼ਦਾਦ ਤੇ ਲੰਕਾ ਤੱਕ ਹਜ਼ਾਰਾਂ ਮੀਲਾਂ ਦਾ ਪੈਂਡਾ ਤੈਅ ਕੀਤਾ। ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਾਗ ਬਿਹਾਗੜਾ ਅਧੀਨ ਆਪ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਤਿੰਨ ਸਲੋਕ ਸੁਸ਼ੋਭਿਤ ਹਨ।

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born as Bura in Kathu Nangal, he met Guru Nanak Dev Ji as a twelve-year-old boy grazing cattle in 1518. Offering fresh milk to the Guru, young Bura questioned him about death and liberation. Guru Nanak marvelled at his wisdom, saying: 'Though a child in age, you speak like an enlightened elder (Buddha)!' From that day, he was known as Baba Buddha. He dedicated his entire 125-year life to selfless service in the Guru's court—clearing fields, cutting timber, digging the sacred pool of Amritsar, and supervising the construction of the Baoli at Goindval. Unique in world spiritual history, Baba Buddha Ji had the supreme honor of performing the ceremonial coronation (Gurgaddi tilak) for five successive Gurus: Guru Angad, Guru Amar Das, Guru Ram Das, Guru Arjan Dev, and Guru Hargobind. In 1604, when Guru Arjan Dev installed the sacred Adi Granth inside Sri Harmandir Sahib, Baba Buddha Ji was appointed the first Head Granthi, ceremoniously opening the scripture and reading the first Hukamnama.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: कथू नंगल के बूड़ा जी १२ वर्ष की आयु में गुरु नानक देव जी से मिले। जब उन्होंने दूध भेंट कर जीवन-मृत्यु का प्रश्न पूछा, तो गुरु जी ने उन्हें 'बुड्ढा' (ज्ञानवृद्ध) की उपाधि दी। उन्होंने १२५ वर्ष के दीर्घ जीवन में पांच गुरुओं को तिलक लगाकर गुरुपद सौंपा। १६०४ में जब हरिमंदिर साहिब में श्री आदि ग्रंथ साहिब का प्रथम प्रकाश हुआ, तो गुरु अर्जुन देव जी ने बाबा बुड्ढा जी को प्रथम मुख्य ग्रंथी नियुक्त किया।
unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਕੱਥੂ ਨੰਗਲ ਦੇ ਬੂੜਾ ਜੀ ਨੇ ੧੨ ਸਾਲ ਦੀ ਉਮਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਦੁੱਧ ਭੇਟ ਕੀਤਾ। ਗੰਭੀਰ ਬਚਨ ਸੁਣ ਕੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੇ 'ਬਾਬਾ ਬੁੱਢਾ' ਦਾ ਖ਼ਿਤਾਬ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਿਆ। ਆਪ ਜੀ ਨੇ ੧੨੫ ਸਾਲ ਦੀ ਉਮਰ ਤੱਕ ਨਿਸ਼ਕਾਮ ਸੇਵਾ ਕੀਤੀ। ਪੰਜ ਗੁਰੂ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਗੁਰਗੱਦੀ ਦਾ ਤਿਲਕ ਲਾਉਣ ਦਾ ਮਾਣ ਆਪ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤ ਹੈ। ੧੬੦੪ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਦਰਬਾਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿਖੇ ਆਦਿ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੇ ਪਹਿਲੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੀ ਥਾਪੇ ਗਏ।

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born in Ghazni (Afghanistan), Bhai Nand Lal was an extraordinary scholar of Persian and Arabic who served as the Mir Munshi (Chief Secretary) to Mughal Prince Muazzam (later Emperor Bahadur Shah). When Emperor Aurangzeb admired Nand Lal's brilliant scholarly interpretation of a difficult Quranic verse, he plotted to forcibly convert him to Islam. Alerted to the danger, Nand Lal fled Delhi and sought sanctuary at Anandpur Sahib in 1682. The moment he gazed upon Guru Gobind Singh, all worldly desires vanished. Refusing any special status, he spent his days serving in the Langar and writing Persian poetry under the pen-name 'Goya' (The Eloquent). His works—including Zindaginama, Ghazaliat, Tauseef-o-Sana, and Rahitnama—are so spiritually pristine that they were granted official canonical sanction to be sung as scripture alongside Gurbani inside Sikh Gurdwaras.

When Bhai Mani Singh was arrested in 1737 for failing to pay the exorbitant jizya tax after the Diwali gathering was sabotaged by imperial troops, Bhai Jagat Singh and several companions stood by his side. Taken to the Nakhas market execution ground of Lahore in June 1738, the Mughal governor ordered Bhai Mani Singh's joints cut one by one. Jagat Singh remained immersed in contemplation of the Guru until his skinless body yielded its final breath.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Father-in-law to Maharaja Duleep Singh, Sardar Chattar Singh was governor of the difficult frontier province of Hazara during the British regency over Lahore. When British political agent Captain James Abbott insulted him, raised Muslim militias to attack Sikh garrisons, and plotted to annex Punjab, Chattar Singh refused to endure humiliation. Defying the British residency, he mobilized the Sikh frontier troops and sounded the call of national liberation across Punjab. unverifiedDraft.journey: Daughter of Guru Angad Dev Ji and Mata Khivi, Bibi Amro was raised in the celestial atmosphere of Khadur Sahib. Blessed with a melodious voice and deep spiritual understanding, she recited Gurbani every dawn while churning buttermilk in her marital home at Basarke. Her father-in-law's brother, the elderly Amar Das, heard her chanting the verses of Asa di Var. The divine hymns pierced his soul like lightning, shattering decades of spiritual wanderings. He begged Bibi Amro to lead him to her father Guru Angad. Thus, she was the sacred bridge that connected the second Guru with the third. Later, when Guru Amar Das established 22 Manjis (missionary administrative centers), he appointed Bibi Amro as the leader of one of the dioceses, giving a woman complete spiritual authority to preach, administer baptism, and guide congregations equally alongside men in the 16th century.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: गुरु अंगद देव जी की पुत्री बीबी अमरो प्रतिदिन अमृतवेले मक्खन बिलोते हुए आसा दी वार का पाठ करती थीं। उनके ससुर के भाई वयोवृद्ध अमर दास जी ने उनकी मधुर वाणी सुनी तो उनका हृदय वैराग्य से भर गया। वे बीबी अमरो के साथ खड़ूर साहिब पहुंचे और गुरु चरणों में लीन हो गए। बाद में जब गुरु अमर दास जी ने २२ मंजियां बनाईं, तो बीबी अमरो को प्रथम महिला मंजीदार (प्रचारक) बनाया गया।

unverifiedDraft.tagline: The ecstatic calico-printer saint whose 61 divine hymns are enshrined in Sri Guru Granth Sahib, for whom God turned the temple doors and revived the dead cow.
unverifiedDraft.taglineLocal: महाराष्ट्र के महान संत जिनके ६१ पावन श्लोक श्री गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में दर्ज हैं, जिनके लिए ईश्वर ने मंदिर का द्वार घुमा दिया था।
unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਮਹਾਰਾਸ਼ਟਰ ਦੇ ਮਹਾਨ ਭਗਤ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ੬੧ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਰਜ ਹਨ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਭਗਤੀ ਲਈ ਰੱਬ ਨੇ ਮੰਦਰ ਦਾ ਦੁਆਰਾ ਘੁਮਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਸੀ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Born into a tailor/calico-printer (Chhimba) family in Narsi-Bamani, Maharashtra, Namdev's devotion was intensely personal. As a child, he offered milk to the deity Vitthala, weeping until the Lord manifested and drank the milk from his bowl. Traveling north, he spent over two decades in the village of Ghuman (Gurdaspur, Punjab), preaching devotion to the Formless One (Nirguna Parabrahma) in the language of the masses. In Delhi, when Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq commanded him to revive a slaughtered cow or face execution under an enraged elephant, Namdev's prayer restored the cow to life, humbling the emperor. In Pandharpur, when caste-proud Brahmins expelled him from the temple for his low birth, Namdev sat behind the outer wall singing hymns; miraculously, the entire temple rotated on its foundation to face Namdev. His 61 hymns, spanning 18 musical rags, form an integral pillar of Sri Guru Granth Sahib.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: महाराष्ट्र में जन्मे भगत नामदेव जी की भक्ति अनन्य थी। बचपन में उनके हठ पर भगवान ने साक्षात कटोरे से दूध पिया था। बाद में उन्होंने पंजाब के घुमाण में २० वर्ष से अधिक समय बिताया और निर्गुण भक्ति का प्रचार किया। सुल्तान द्वारा गाय जीवित करने की परीक्षा में वे सफल रहे। जब पंडितों ने जाति के नाम पर उन्हें मंदिर से निकाला, तो भगवान ने मंदिर का मुख नामदेव की ओर घुमा दिया। श्री गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में उनके ६१ पद सुशोभित हैं।
unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਮਹਾਰਾਸ਼ਟਰ ਦੇ ਛੀਂਬਾ ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਜਨਮੇ ਭਗਤ ਨਾਮਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਬਚਪਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਥੀਂ ਦੁੱਧ ਪਿਲਾਇਆ। ਆਪ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇ ਪਿੰਡ ਘੁਮਾਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਲੰਮਾ ਸਮਾਂ ਗੁਜ਼ਾਰਿਆ। ਦਿੱਲੀ ਦੇ ਬਾਦਸ਼ਾਹ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਮੋਈ ਗਾਂ ਜਿਊਂਦੀ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਸਫਲ ਹੋਏ। ਜਦੋਂ ਹੰਕਾਰੀ ਪੁਜਾਰੀਆਂ ਨੇ ਮੰਦਰ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਕੱਢਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਭਗਵਾਨ ਨੇ ਮੰਦਰ ਦਾ ਮੂੰਹ ਨਾਮਦੇਵ ਵੱਲ ਮੋੜ ਦਿੱਤਾ। ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪ ਜੀ ਦੇ ੬੧ ਸ਼ਬਦ ੧੮ ਰਾਗਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਰਜ ਹਨ।

unverifiedDraft.taglineLocal: काशी के परम संत जिन्होंने जूते गांठते हुए ईश्वर का साक्षात्कार किया, जिनके ४० पद गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में दर्ज हैं और जिन्होंने 'बेगमपुरा' का शाश्वत संदेश दिया।
unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਕਾਸ਼ੀ ਦੇ ਮਹਾਨ ਸੰਤ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਜੁੱਤੀਆਂ ਗੰਢਦਿਆਂ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਭਗਤੀ ਕੀਤੀ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ੪੦ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਰਜ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ 'ਬੇਗਮਪੁਰਾ' ਦਾ ਸੰਕਲਪ ਦਿੱਤਾ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Born into an untouchable Chamar family in Varanasi, Ravidas spent his days tanning hides and repairing worn footwear. Yet his heart was steeped in the nectar of divine communion. He treated his humble craft as sacred worship: when customers offered coins, he often gave them shoes for free, using water from his leather-working vat to bless seekers. Royal sovereigns, including Queen Mirabai and Rana Sanga of Mewar, bowed at his feet as his disciples. When orthodox Brahmins complained that an outcaste could not touch sacred shaligram stones, Ravidas opened his chest to reveal the glowing golden thread of spiritual realization within his heart. His 40 sublime hymns in Sri Guru Granth Sahib articulate 'Begampura'—a revolutionary society completely free of grief, taxation, caste oppression, fear, and inequality.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: वाराणसी में जन्मे संत रविदास जूते बनाने का कार्य करते हुए निरंतर ईश्वर-ध्यान में लीन रहते थे। उनका कहना था 'मन चंगा तो कठौती में गंगा'। मीराबाई और मेवाड़ के राजाओं ने उनका शिष्यत्व ग्रहण किया। जब रूढ़िवादी पंडितों ने उनकी जाति का उपहास किया, तो उन्होंने सिद्ध किया कि ईश्वर केवल प्रेम का भूखा है। श्री गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में उनके ४० पावन पद संकलित हैं, जिनमें उन्होंने 'बेगमपुरा' (दुख-रहित समतामूलक समाज) का दिव्य दर्शन दिया।

unverifiedDraft.journey: Raised by a Muslim weaver family in Varanasi, Kabir lived as a humble craftsman weaving cloth on his handloom while continuously spinning the thread of divine remembrance. A fearless challenger of institutional religious fraud, he lashed out equally at corrupt Hindu pandits and tyrannical Muslim qazis for replacing inner compassion with empty rituals. When orthodox clerics threw him bound in chains before a rogue elephant in Delhi, the elephant bowed and refused to crush him. When they threw him into the rushing Ganges tied to heavy stones, the bonds broke and he floated serenely on the surface. To shatter the superstition that dying in Kashi bestows heaven while dying in Maghar brings rebirth as an ass, Kabir intentionally walked to Maghar in his final days and left his mortal frame there. With 541 hymns across 17 rags, Bhagat Kabir's fearless voice resounds through Sri Guru Granth Sahib as an eternal manifesto of spiritual rebellion.

unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਕਾਸ਼ੀ ਦੇ ਜੁਲਾਹੇ ਭਗਤ ਕਬੀਰ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਖੱਡੀ ਉਣਦਿਆਂ-ਉਣਦਿਆਂ ਨਾਮ ਦੀ ਕਮਾਈ ਕੀਤੀ। ਪੰਡਿਤਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਕਾਜ਼ੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਪਾਖੰਡਾਂ ਦਾ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹ ਕੇ ਵਿਰੋਧ ਕੀਤਾ। ਸਿਕੰਦਰ ਲੋਦੀ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਗੰਗਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਡੋਬਣ ਅਤੇ ਮਸਤ ਹਾਥੀ ਅੱਗੇ ਸੁੱਟਣ ਦੇ ਤਸੀਹੇ ਝੱਲੇ ਪਰ ਅਡੋਲ ਰਹੇ। ਕਾਸ਼ੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਰਨ ਨਾਲ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਮਗਹਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਰਨ ਨਾਲ ਖੋਤਾ ਬਣਨ ਦੇ ਅੰਧ-ਵਿਸ਼ਵਾਸ ਨੂੰ ਤੋੜਨ ਲਈ ਅਖ਼ੀਰਲੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਮਗਹਰ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਪ੍ਰਾਣ ਤਿਆਗੇ। ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪ ਜੀ ਦੇ ੫੪੧ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਸੁਸ਼ੋਭਿਤ ਹਨ।

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born in Kothewal near Multan, Khwaja Fariduddin Masud was affectionately called 'Ganj-i-Shakar' (Treasury of Sugar) because his mother placed lumps of sugar beneath his prayer mat to encourage his childhood prayers, until God miraculously turned sand into sweet sugar for the young ascetic. Farid spent years in intense desert austerities at Pakpattan (Ajodhan), subsisting on wild berries and dry bread with wooden crusts. Guru Nanak Dev Ji preserved his pure Punjabi poetry, which was later incorporated into Sri Guru Granth Sahib by Guru Arjan Dev. Farid's 134 Sloks in Gurbani are world-renowned for their soul-stirring reflections on the brevity of human life, the inexorable reality of death, the necessity of sweet speech, and forgiving one's enemies. When someone gifted him a sharp pair of scissors, Farid gently handed them back, saying: 'Bring me a needle, not scissors; my work is to sew hearts together, not to cut them apart!'

unverifiedDraft.trialPa: ਜੰਗਲਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਰੁੱਖੀ-ਮਿੱਸੀ ਖਾ ਕੇ ਅਤੇ ਖੂਹ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਲਟੇ ਲਟਕ ਕੇ ਚਿੱਲੇ ਕੱਟਣੇ ਤੇ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਾਬੂ ਕਰਨਾ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦਾ ਵੱਡਾ ਤਪ ਸੀ।
unverifiedDraft.teaching: Do not speak ill of anyone, for the True Beloved dwells in every soul; do not break any human heart, for every heart is a precious jewel.
unverifiedDraft.teachingLocal: इकु फिकानु गालाइ सभना मैं सच्चा धणी; किसी का दिल मत दुखाओ, क्योंकि हर हृदय में परमात्मा स्वयं निवास करता है।
unverifiedDraft.teachingPa: ਇਕੁ ਫਿਕਾ ਨ ਗਾਲਾਇ ਸਭਨਾ ਮੈ ਸਚਾ ਧਣੀ ॥ ਹਿਆਉ ਨ ਕੈਹੀ ਠਾਹਿ ਮਾਣਕ ਸਭ ਅਮੋਲਵੈ ॥
unverifiedDraft.moral: Sweetness of tongue, patience under suffering, and loving forgiveness toward those who harm you constitute the highest sanctity.
unverifiedDraft.moralLocal: मीठी वाणी, क्षमा और बुरा करने वाले का भी भला करना ही ईश्वर-प्राप्ति का सच्चा मार्ग है।
unverifiedDraft.moralPa: ਮਿੱਠਾ ਬੋਲਣਾ, ਬੁਰਾ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਦਾ ਵੀ ਭਲਾ ਕਰਨਾ ਅਤੇ ਹਿਰਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਰੱਖਣੀ ਹੀ ਸੱਚੀ ਦਰਵੇਸ਼ੀ ਹੈ।
unverifiedDraft.legacy: Father of Punjabi poetic literature and revered Sufi saint whose divine verses in Sri Guru Granth Sahib form an eternal bond between Sufism and Sikhi.
unverifiedDraft.legacyLocal: पंजाबी साहित्य के जनक और श्री गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में प्रतिष्ठित महान संत जिन्होंने सूफी मत और गुरमत को प्रेम से जोड़ा।
unverifiedDraft.legacyPa: ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਸ਼ਾਇਰੀ ਦੇ ਪਿਤਾਮਾ ਅਤੇ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਰਜ ਮਹਾਨ ਸੂਫ਼ੀ ਦਰਵੇਸ਼।

name: Bhagat Dhanna Ji

unverifiedDraft.tagline: The simple Jat farmer from Rajasthan whose childlike, pure faith compelled God to manifest directly from a stone and plow his agricultural fields.
unverifiedDraft.taglineLocal: राजस्थान के सरल किसान जिनकी बाल-सुलभ निष्कपट भक्ति के कारण परमात्मा ने पत्थर से प्रकट होकर उनके खेतों में हल चलाया।
unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਰਾਜਸਥਾਨ ਦੇ ਭੋਲੇ-ਭਾਲੇ ਕਿਸਾਨ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਨਿਰਛਲ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਸਦਕਾ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਤਮਾ ਨੇ ਪੱਥਰ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਪ੍ਰਗਟ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੇ ਖੇਤਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਲ਼ ਵਾਹਿਆ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Born into a simple Jat farming family in the village of Dhuwan (Rajasthan), Dhanna observed a Brahmin neighbor worshipping a stone idol and feeding it food. Dhanna asked for a stone to worship. The Brahmin, annoyed, gave him an ordinary rough field stone. Dhanna took the stone home, washed it lovingly, and prepared warm rotis and butter. He placed the food before the stone, saying: 'O Lord, eat this bread! I will not touch a single morsel until you have eaten.' Days passed; Dhanna starved, weeping in childlike simplicity. Moved by his flawless devotion, the Supreme Lord materialized in divine physical form, ate the bread with joy, and gave the blessed leftovers to Dhanna. God remained so enchanted by Dhanna's unpretentious love that the Lord Himself plowed his fields, harvested his crops, and filled his granaries. His four hymns inside Sri Guru Granth Sahib celebrate how pure, uneducated devotion unlocks the highest gates of liberation.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: राजस्थान के टोंक में जन्मे धन्ना जी एक सीधे-सादे किसान थे। पंडित द्वारा दिए गए साधारण पत्थर को वे साक्षात ईश्वर मान बैठे। उन्होंने भोजन बनाकर पत्थर के सामने रख दिया और प्रण लिया कि जब तक भगवान भोजन नहीं करेंगे, वे भी अन्न ग्रहण नहीं करेंगे। कई दिनों के उपवास के बाद उनकी निष्कपट भक्ति से द्रवित होकर ईश्वर ने प्रकट होकर भोजन किया। भगवान ने उनके खेतों में हल चलाया। श्री गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में उनके पावन पद संकलित हैं।
unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਰਾਜਸਥਾਨ ਦੇ ਪਿੰਡ ਧੂਆਨ ਦੇ ਰਹਿਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਭਗਤ ਧੰਨਾ ਜੀ ਸਿੱਧੇ-ਸਾਦੇ ਜੱਟ ਕਿਸਾਨ ਸਨ। ਪੰਡਿਤ ਕੋਲੋਂ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਮੰਗਣ 'ਤੇ ਉਸਨੇ ਇੱਕ ਸਾਧਾਰਨ ਪੱਥਰ ਫੜਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ। ਧੰਨਾ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਘਰ ਆ ਕੇ ਰੋਟੀ ਪਕਾਈ ਅਤੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਰੱਖ ਕੇ ਬੈਠ ਗਏ ਕਿ ਜਦੋਂ ਤੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨਹੀਂ ਛਕਣਗੇ, ਮੈਂ ਵੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਛਕਾਂਗਾ। ਭੋਲੇ ਭਾਅ ਭਗਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਖ਼ੁਸ਼ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਤਮਾ ਨੇ ਪ੍ਰਗਟ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਭੋਜਨ ਛਕਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਖੇਤਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪ ਹਲ਼ ਵਾਹਿਆ। ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਚਾਰ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਸੁਸ਼ੋਭਿਤ ਹਨ।
unverifiedDraft.trial: Starving for days in innocent refusal to eat until an inanimate stone manifested the living presence of God.
unverifiedDraft.trialLocal: अन्न-जल त्यागकर बाल-हठ के साथ पत्थर से साक्षात ईश्वर को प्रकट करने का संकल्प उनकी अगाध निष्ठा की परीक्षा थी।
unverifiedDraft.trialPa: ਪੱਥਰ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਰੱਬ ਨੂੰ ਪ੍ਰਤੱਖ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਕਈ ਦਿਨ ਭੁੱਖੇ-ਪਿਆਸੇ ਬੈਠੇ ਰਹਿਣਾ ਅਟੱਲ ਭਰੋਸੇ ਦੀ ਪਰਖ ਸੀ।
unverifiedDraft.teaching: God is attained through innocent, guileless love (Bhole bhaav mile kartar), not through convoluted scholarly rituals.
unverifiedDraft.teachingLocal: परमात्मा कपटहीन, सरल प्रेम से मिलता है; कर्मकांड और पाखंड से प्रभु की प्राप्ति असंभव है।
unverifiedDraft.teachingPa: ਭੋਲੇ ਭਾਇ ਮਿਲੇ ਰਘੁਰਾਇਆ। ਰੱਬ ਕਿਸੇ ਪਾਖੰਡ ਨਾਲ ਨਹੀਂ, ਸਗੋਂ ਸਾਫ਼ ਦਿਲ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਰਛਲ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਦਾ ਹੈ।
unverifiedDraft.moral: Simplicity and total trust in God achieve what decades of proud scholarly meditation fail to grasp.
unverifiedDraft.moralLocal: सरल और निष्कपट विश्वास वह सब प्राप्त कर लेता है जो प्रकांड विद्वानों को भी दुर्लभ होता है।
unverifiedDraft.moralPa: ਨਿਰਛਲ ਭਰੋਸਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਦਗੀ ਵੱਡੇ-ਵੱਡੇ ਵਿਦਵਾਨਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਵੀ ਵੱਡੀ ਆਤਮਿਕ ਤਾਕਤ ਹੈ।
unverifiedDraft.legacy: Immortalized in Sri Guru Granth Sahib as the archetype of 'Bhole Bhaav' devotion, proving that farmers and laborers are closest to the Divine.
unverifiedDraft.legacyLocal: श्री गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में प्रतिष्ठित, जिन्होंने सिद्ध किया कि किसान और श्रमिक अपनी निष्कपटता से ईश्वर के सबसे निकट हैं।
unverifiedDraft.legacyPa: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਰਜ ਭਗਤ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਸਾਬਤ ਕੀਤਾ ਕਿ ਮਿਹਨਤਕਸ਼ ਕਿਸਾਨ ਰੱਬ ਦੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਨੇੜੇ ਹੁੰਦੇ ਹਨ।

name: Bhagat Pipa Ji

unverifiedDraft.tagline: The royal Rajput King of Gagron who renounced his throne and vast imperial wealth to become an ascetic saint of Ramananda, whose divine hymn is preserved in Sri Guru Granth Sahib.
unverifiedDraft.taglineLocal: गागरोन के राजपूत राजा जिन्होंने राजवैभव त्यागकर स्वामी रामानंद से दीक्षा ली और जिनका पावन पद श्री गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में दर्ज है।
unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਗਾਗਰੋਨ ਦੇ ਰਾਜਪੂਤ ਰਾਜਾ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਰਾਜ-ਭਾਗ ਤਿਆਗ ਕੇ ਸੰਤ ਰਾਮਾਨੰਦ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਰਨ ਲਈ, ਅਤੇ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦਾ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਰਜ ਹੈ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: King Pipa was the ruler of the impregnable hill-and-water fort of Gagron in Rajasthan. A sovereign of great wealth and power, he was a worshipper of Goddess Bhavani. An inner spiritual voice directed him to seek initiation from the great Vaishnava master Swami Ramananda in Varanasi. When Pipa arrived in royal pomp, Ramananda refused to see him, sending word: 'My door is for beggars, not kings!' Pipa immediately gave away his royal treasures to the poor, donned simple ascetic robes, and returned. Ramananda tested him by commanding: 'Jump into that well!' Pipa sprinted toward the well to leap, but disciples caught him. Convinced of his total surrender, Ramananda initiated him. Pipa abdicated his throne, accompanied only by his devout queen Sita, and wandered across India preaching equality and divine contemplation. His sublime hymn in Sri Guru Granth Sahib in Rag Dhanasari proclaims that the Creator is found within the human body itself, rendering outer pilgrimages unnecessary.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: गागरोन के राजा पीपा संपन्न शासक थे। आत्मिक शांति हेतु वे काशी में स्वामी रामानंद की शरण में पहुंचे। रामानंद जी ने राजा होने के कारण मिलने से मना किया तो पीपा ने सर्वस्व दान कर दिया और फकीरी वस्त्र धारण कर लिए। गुरु की आज्ञा पर कुएं में कूदने को तत्पर होने पर रामानंद जी ने उन्हें शिष्य बनाया। उन्होंने राजपाट त्याग दिया और अपनी रानी सीता के साथ निष्काम भक्ति में लीन हो गए। गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में राग धनासरी में उनका पावन पद दर्ज है।
unverifiedDraft.journeyPa: ਗਾਗਰੋਨ ਦੇ ਰਾਜਪੂਤ ਰਾਜਾ ਪੀਪਾ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਰੂਹਾਨੀ ਖੋਜ ਲਈ ਕਾਸ਼ੀ ਵਿਖੇ ਸਵਾਮੀ ਰਾਮਾਨੰਦ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਰਨ ਲਈ। ਰਾਜਸੀ ਠਾਠ-ਬਾਠ ਤਿਆਗ ਕੇ ਗਰੀਬਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਭ ਕੁਝ ਵੰਡ ਦਿੱਤਾ। ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਆਗਿਆ 'ਤੇ ਖੂਹ ਵਿੱਚ ਛਾਲ ਮਾਰਨ ਲਈ ਤਿਆਰ ਹੋਣ 'ਤੇ ਰਾਮਾਨੰਦ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਸੀਨੇ ਨਾਲ ਲਾਇਆ। ਆਪ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਰਾਜ-ਭਾਗ ਛੱਡ ਕੇ ਫ਼ਕੀਰੀ ਧਾਰਨ ਕੀਤੀ। ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਾਗ ਧਨਾਸਰੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਦਰਜ ਹੈ ਜਿਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪ ਨੇ ਸਰੀਰ ਨੂੰ ਹੀ ਰੱਬ ਦਾ ਮੰਦਰ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਹੈ।
unverifiedDraft.trial: Abdicating an impregnable royal fortress and boundless wealth to wander penniless across India as an ascetic.
unverifiedDraft.trialLocal: राजसी सुख, सेना और सिंहासन को लात मारकर ईश्वर-प्राप्ति हेतु भिक्षुक का जीवन स्वीकार करना उनका सर्वोच्च त्याग था।
unverifiedDraft.trialPa: ਸੋਨੇ ਦਾ ਤਖ਼ਤ ਅਤੇ ਰਾਜਸੀ ਸੁੱਖ ਤਿਆਗ ਕੇ ਧੂੜ ਭਰੇ ਰਾਹਾਂ 'ਤੇ ਨੰਗੇ ਪੈਰੀਂ ਫ਼ਕੀਰ ਬਣ ਕੇ ਤੁਰਨਾ ਅਲੌਕਿਕ ਤਿਆਗ ਸੀ।
unverifiedDraft.teaching: Whatever is in the entire cosmos is also within this physical body; whoever searches within will discover the Supreme Lord.
unverifiedDraft.teachingLocal: जो ब्रह्मांड में है, वही इस शरीर में है; जो अंतर्मुखी होकर खोजता है, वही परमात्मा को प्राप्त करता है।
unverifiedDraft.teachingPa: ਜੋ ਬ੍ਰਹਮੰਡੇ ਸੋਈ ਪਿੰਡੇ ਜੋ ਖੋਜੈ ਸੋ ਪਾਵੈ। ਤੀਰਥਾਂ 'ਤੇ ਭਟਕਣ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨਹੀਂ, ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਘਟ-ਘਟ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ।
unverifiedDraft.moral: True sovereignty is conquering one's own desires and ego, not ruling over earthly territories.
unverifiedDraft.moralLocal: सच्ची बादशाही अपने मन और विकारों को जीतने में है, न कि भूभाग पर राज करने में।
unverifiedDraft.moralPa: ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਜਿੱਤਣਾ ਹੀ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੀ ਬਾਦਸ਼ਾਹੀ ਹੈ; ਦੁਨਿਆਵੀ ਰਾਜ-ਭਾਗ ਨਾਸ਼ਵੰਤ ਹਨ।
unverifiedDraft.legacy: Enshrined in Sri Guru Granth Sahib, immortal example of royal renunciation in pursuit of universal spiritual truth.
unverifiedDraft.legacyLocal: श्री गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में अमर, राजसी त्याग और आत्म-साक्षात्कार के अनुपम आदर्श।
unverifiedDraft.legacyPa: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਰਜ ਭਗਤ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਰਾਜ-ਭਾਗ ਤਿਆਗ ਕੇ ਸਿੱਖੀ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ 'ਤੇ ਪਹਿਰਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ।

name: Bhagat Sain Ji

unverifiedDraft.tagline: The humble royal barber of Rewa whose loving devotion was so dear to God that the Divine assumed his form and gave a royal oil massage to the king while Sain served holy saints.
unverifiedDraft.taglineLocal: रीवा के सरल नाई-संत जिनकी भक्ति से प्रसन्न होकर ईश्वर ने स्वयं उनका रूप धारण कर राजा की मालिश की, जब सैन जी संतों की सेवा में लीन थे।
unverifiedDraft.taglinePa: ਰੀਵਾ ਰਿਆਸਤ ਦੇ ਉਹ ਭਗਤ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਭਗਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਖ਼ੁਸ਼ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਤਮਾ ਨੇ ਆਪ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦਾ ਰੂਪ ਧਾਰ ਕੇ ਰਾਜੇ ਦੀ ਮਾਲਸ਼ ਕੀਤੀ, ਜਦੋਂ ਸੈਣ ਜੀ ਸਾਧੂਆਂ ਦੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਰੁੱਝੇ ਸਨ।
unverifiedDraft.journey: Born into a barber (Nai) family, Sain served as the personal barber and masseur to Raja Ram, the ruler of Rewa. A disciple of Swami Ramananda, Sain's house was always open to visiting holy ascetics. One morning, as he was preparing to attend to the king, a group of saintly mendicants arrived at his cottage. Sain became completely absorbed in washing their feet, preparing food, and singing hymns with them, completely forgetting his duty at the royal court. Seeing His devotee's dilemma, God assumed the exact physical form and voice of Sain, went to the palace, and massaged the king's body with fragrant oils. The king felt such transcendent bliss and peace that he had never experienced before. Later, when the real Sain rushed to the palace trembling with fear of punishment and apologized, the king exclaimed: 'Why do you apologize? The touch of your hands today filled my soul with divine ecstasy!' When Sain realized that the Lord Himself had served the king in his guise, he wept in gratitude. His hymn is enshrined in Sri Guru Granth Sahib in Rag Dhanasari.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born in Sarabha village near Ludhiana, Kartar Singh went to the United States in 1912 at age fifteen to study engineering at UC Berkeley. The racial humiliations suffered by Indians abroad radicalized him. Alongside Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna, he became the youngest founding member and chief editor of the revolutionary Ghadar newspaper, printing revolutionary poetry by night and organizing workers by day. When World War I began, he sailed back to India to spark an armed rebellion within the British Indian Army. Traversing Punjab disguised on a bicycle, he persuaded dozens of military cantonments to revolt. Betrayed by an undercover police spy Kirpal Singh, he was captured. At his trial in the Lahore Conspiracy Case, nineteen-year-old Kartar Singh astonished British judges by boldly confessing: 'I have waged war against King-Emperor George V. My only regret is that the rebellion failed. Hang me immediately so I can be reborn to fight for India's freedom again!' On November 16, 1915, he walked to the gallows of Central Jail Lahore singing patriotic songs.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Orphaned in childhood and raised in the Central Khalsa Orphanage at Amritsar, Udham Singh was serving water to peaceful pilgrims in Jallianwala Bagh on Baisakhi day, April 13, 1919, when General Dyer's troops massacred over a thousand innocent men, women, and children. Smearing the blood-soaked earth onto his forehead, Udham Singh swore an eternal oath to punish Sir Michael O'Dwyer, the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab who ordered and celebrated the massacre. For twenty-one years, living under forged passports and pseudonyms, he crossed Africa, Europe, and America, working as a carpenter, mechanic, and extra in films, patiently stalking his target. On March 13, 1940, inside London's Caxton Hall, Udham Singh drew a revolver from a hollowed-out book and shot O'Dwyer dead. He made no attempt to flee, holding his arms out for arrest. unverifiedDraft.journey: Born Basant Singh in Narangwal (Ludhiana), he gave up government service after taking Amrit in 1904. He participated in the Rakab Ganj Gurdwara boundary wall agitation and joined the Ghadar rebellion in 1914 to liberate India by force of arms. Arrested in the Ferozepur cantonment raid in 1915, he was sentenced to life imprisonment in the Second Lahore Conspiracy Case and transported to the Andaman cellular jail and various harsh mainland prisons. For sixteen long years, British jailers attempted to break his spirit: he was kept in pitch-black solitary confinement, force-fed beef soup by wardens (which he vomited out and fasted for 40 days until provided pure vegetarian grain), and subjected to icy water torture. Through every trial, Bhai Randhir Singh remained seated in deep meditation, radiating unbroken joy through Akhand Kirtan and divine contemplation. When released in 1930, he met Shaheed Bhagat Singh in Lahore Central Jail, inspiring him with spiritual dialogue. He founded the Akhand Kirtani Jatha and authored over two dozen profound theological works.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Grandson of the Sikh scholar Mahant Tara Singh and son of Dr. Charan Singh, Bhai Vir Singh was born in Amritsar during the critical period when Christian missionaries and colonial schools were aggressively proselytizing Punjab's youth. Seeing the identity of the Khalsa evaporating, Vir Singh resolved to launch a cultural and intellectual renaissance. In 1892, he established the Wazir Hind Press, the first Punjabi printing press in Amritsar, and co-founded the Khalsa Tract Society. He wrote classic historical novels—Sundari (1898, the very first Punjabi novel), Bijay Singh, Satwant Kaur, and Baba Naudh Singh—which depicted the supreme courage and moral purity of 18th-century Sikhs, sparking an electrifying revival of Sikh pride across the globe. He founded the weekly newspaper Khalsa Samachar, edited the monumental 14-volume Sri Gur Pratap Suraj Granth, and composed immortal mystical poetry (Rana Surat Singh, Matak Hulare) that earned him the Sahitya Akademi Award and Padma Bhushan.

unverifiedDraft.journey: Born into a scholarly lineage in Nabha, Kahn Singh studied Sanskrit, Persian, Arabic, and music, mastering classical scriptures alongside Western philosophy. He served as the Chief Minister and tutor in the princely state of Nabha. When Max Arthur Macauliffe undertook the monumental task of translating Sikh religion and scripture into English (The Sikh Religion, 6 volumes), it was Bhai Kahn Singh who spent months in London guiding Macauliffe through the intricate linguistic idioms of Gurbani. In 1898, he penned the seminal theological manifesto 'Ham Hindu Nahin', defining the distinct, sovereign theological identity of the Sikh faith. His magnum opus was the Gurshabad Ratnakar Mahan Kosh (Encyclopaedia of Sikh Literature), containing 64,263 entries covering every theological, geographical, historical, and mythological reference across Sikh scriptures and chronicles. Begun in 1912 and completed in 1926, it remains the undisputed supreme reference encyclopedia of Sikhism for over a century.
unverifiedDraft.journeyLocal: नाभा के प्रकांड विद्वान भाई काह्न सिंह ने संस्कृत, फारसी और अरबी का गहन अध्ययन किया। वे नाभा रियासत के मुख्य प्रशासक रहे। उन्होंने मैक्स आर्थर मैकालिफ को सिख धर्मग्रंथों का अंग्रेजी अनुवाद करने में मार्गदर्शन दिया। १८९८ में उन्होंने ऐतिहासिक पुस्तक 'हम हिंदू नहीं' लिखकर सिख धर्म की स्वतंत्र धार्मिक पहचान को रेखांकित किया। उनका सर्वोच्च कार्य 'महान कोश' (सिख साहित्य का विश्वकोश) है, जिसमें ६४,२६३ प्रविष्टियां हैं। यह ग्रंथ आज भी सिख धर्म का सबसे प्रामाणिक शब्दकोश है।
